channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Planalto vê ‘dobradinha’ entre Marco Rubio e Flávio Bolsonaro após anúncio de ‘tarifaço’
item.description: Plano Palace officials assessed that Flávio Bolsonaro formed a 'double act' with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to blame President Lula for Trump’s 25% tariff hike. The move suggests a coordinated opposition strategy to link the Brazilian government to economically unpopular external measures.

item.title: As propostas de Zema para aumentar o crescimento
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and pre-candidate for the 2026 presidency, argued that Brazil has a competitive productive sector but is hindered by excessive bureaucracy, high tax burden, and an oversized state. He proposed reducing ministries to around 20, privatizing state-owned enterprises, expanding the Simples Nacional tax regime, lowering taxes on businesses, and increasing concessions and PPPs, advocating for a lean government focused on security, health, and education. Zema emphasized that the 'Brazil cost' destroys R$1.7 trillion annually and that entrepreneurs succeed despite a hostile business environment marked by interest rates above 14%, outdated labor laws, and poor logistics infrastructure.

item.title: Boulos diz que “porta-vozes do Lula” têm missão de se opor ao tarifaço
item.description: Guilherme Boulos accused Flávio Bolsonaro of co-responsibility for the 25% tariff imposed by the U.S. on Brazilian goods, claiming the senator acted for electoral gain and betrayal of the nation. He urged Lula supporters to counter the narrative on social media and in public spaces, advocating for the Reciprocity Law and rejecting U.S. claims of bad faith by the Itamaraty.

item.title: TSE manda retirar vídeo de influenciador petista que associa Flávio ao PCC
item.description: TSE President Justice Kassio Nunes Marques ordered the removal of a video published on Plantão Brasil and YouTube that linked Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for President, to crimes including money laundering, embezzlement, foreign exchange evasion, and ties to the PCC. The decision followed a complaint alleging defamatory and false content that could influence the electoral process. The TSE reaffirms its role in combating disinformation during elections.

item.title: Nunes Marques derruba vídeo que associa Flávio Bolsonaro ao PCC
item.description: TSE President Minister Kassio Nunes Marques ordered the removal of a video and post from the Plantão Brasil channel that linked Flávio Bolsonaro to the PCC, ruling the content as misinformation with potential to harm the electoral process. The decision cited the lack of evidence connecting the senator to crimes such as money laundering or criminal association, and was driven by the video’s rapid reach during the pre-campaign period.

item.title: Lindbergh cita reciprocidade e "traidores da pátria": "Tariflávio"
item.description: Deputy Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) accused Senators Flávio and Eduardo Bolsonaro of being 'traitors of the homeland' for supporting the 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian products, labeling the measure 'Tariflávio'. He defended Brazil's 'Reciprocity Law' as a tool to retaliate against unilateral foreign measures and claimed that Bolsonarism represents a political group working against national interests.

item.title: O desafio de Flávio para se descolar do tarifaço
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is facing increasing political pressure over the U.S. tariff on Brazilian exports, with 51% of the public blaming him for the measure, according to a Quaest poll, while only 30% blame President Lula. His contradictory explanations regarding a controversial photo alongside an alleged associate of Vorcaro — first claiming he didn’t know the man, then retracting that statement — have fueled accusations of opacity. Meanwhile, PL allies and Nikolas Ferreira attempt to blame Lula with slogans like 'Make the L', but these have failed to gain traction on social media, where pro-Lula counter-slogans dominate.

item.title: Kassio manda excluir do YouTube vídeo de influenciador contra Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques ordered the removal of a YouTube video by influencer Thiago dos Reis (Plantão Brasil channel) linking the Bolsonaro family to the PCC, with a 24-hour deadline and potential fines for non-compliance. The ruling partially granted a request by Flávio Bolsonaro, who claimed the video damaged his reputation and misled voters during the pre-campaign period. The court determined the content asserted proven criminal ties, which does not constitute protected political speech under electoral law.

item.title: Tarifaço dos EUA de 25% sobre produtos brasileiros começa em 22 de julho
item.description: The U.S. will impose a 25% tariff on Brazilian products starting July 22, 2026, excluding beef, coffee and other items, following a Section 301 investigation by the USTR. The measure, part of Trump's 'America First' policy, accuses Brazil of unfair trade practices, including issues related to Pix, digital trade, and illegal deforestation. The Lula government is evaluating responses, including possible retaliatory actions.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: Tarifaço reduz vontade de votar em Flávio, e maioria concorda com versões de Lula
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll reveals that 51% of Brazilians believe Flávio Bolsonaro requested the new U.S. tariffs on Brazil, aligning with Lula’s version, while only 30% think he tried to stop them. A majority (46%) agree with Lula that the tariffs are retaliation against Pix, and trust in Lula has grown, while voting intention for Flávio Bolsonaro has declined among right-wing and Bolsonarist voters due to the tariff’s impact.

item.title: Tarifaço dos EUA prejudica Flávio até entre eleitores de direita
item.description: The new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian products reduced voting intentions for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro from 30% to 27%, even among right-wing voters, while Lula rose from 39% to 42%. The decline was sharper among non-bolsonarista right-wing voters (70% to 60%) and bolsonaristas (88% to 81%), with increased support for 'another candidate' in both groups.

item.title: A dificuldade da PF em ouvir Flávio Bolsonaro em inquérito
item.description: The Federal Police failed to take Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's testimony within the 10-day deadline set by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, despite having contacted his defense from the first day and offering a videoconference. The senator's lawyers cited scheduling conflicts due to his pre-campaign presidential activities and requested a longer deadline and new dates with reasonable notice. The investigation concerns alleged slander against President Lula, based on Flávio's post linking Lula to international drug and arms trafficking, money laundering, support for terrorists and dictatorships, and fraudulent elections, allegedly based on statements by Nicolás Maduro.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro pede mais tempo para depor à PF sobre calúnia contra Lula
item.description: Lawyers for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro have requested a new deadline from the Federal Police for him to testify in the investigation into alleged slander against President Lula, arguing that the ten-day deadline set by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes is too short given his pre-campaign commitments. They claim there is no risk of prescription and that changing the deadline would not hinder the investigation.

item.title: Tarifaço aumenta vontade do eleitor de votar em Lula, diz pesquisa Genial/Quaest
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll released on Thursday (16) shows that the U.S. tariff increase boosted voter inclination to support Lula, with 42% of respondents saying the episode made them more likely to vote for the president. Most interviewees (57%) were unaware of Flávio Bolsonaro’s trip to the U.S. to meet Trump, and 58% believe the senator lacks the power to reverse the tariff. On responsibility for the tariff, 51% agreed with Lula, while only 30% sided with Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Trump não é bom cabo eleitoral, indica pesquisa
item.description: A PoderData/Aya survey shows that 42% of Brazilian voters believe an eventual endorsement by Donald Trump for a presidential candidate would have a negative impact, while only 32% see a positive effect. This suggests Trump is perceived more as a liability than an asset in the context of Brazil's 2026 presidential election.

item.title: Caiado critica Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro após confirmação do tarifaço
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), a pre-candidate for President, criticized President Lula (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) after the confirmation of a 25% tariff imposed by the United States on over 4,000 Brazilian products. In a social media video, Caiado blamed the measure on the federal government's lack of strategy and Congressional inaction, including opposition lawmakers like Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: EBC recorre ao TSE contra retirada de conteúdo durante eleições
item.description: EBC appealed to the TSE to secure the right to publish Agência Brasil reports during the electoral period, after removing over 100,000 political and governmental publications following directives from Secom/PR, AGU, and its own legal counsel under the 'electoral defeso'. The company maintains its content is journalistic, not institutional advertising, and requests objective criteria to distinguish the two. Journalists and press unions condemned the removal as censorship and protested in defense of editorial autonomy.

item.title: Brasil avalia retaliação contra EUA com foco em patentes farmacêuticas e setor audiovisual, diz agência
item.description: The Brazilian government is evaluating retaliatory measures against new U.S. tariffs, focusing on pharmaceutical patents and the audiovisual sector, including potential patent breaks and restrictions on royalty remittances. Discussions are underway in meetings at the Planalto Palace, with President Lula set to decide the final response after consulting affected sectors to avoid inflationary impacts or disruption to production chains.

item.title: Governo de Tarcísio em SP é frouxo e pouco transparente, afirma Haddad
item.description: Fernando Haddad, the PT's pre-candidate for governor of São Paulo and former Finance Minister, criticized Tarcísio de Freitas' administration as 'lax, lacking transparency and insufficiently monitored,' citing corruption hotspots in the Finance, Agriculture, and Transportation secretariats.

item.title: Negociação, OMC e retaliação: como funciona a Lei da Reciprocidade acionada pelo governo após tarifaço
item.description: The Lula government announced it will activate the Reciprocity Law in response to the new 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods. The law allows Camex to suspend trade concessions, apply extra taxes, and restrict imports, but requires direct negotiation and WTO recourse before retaliation, which must be proportional to economic harm. Brazil had previously brought the issue to the WTO in August 2024 over Trump’s initial 50% tariff.

item.title: ‘A culpa é do Lula’: aliados de Flávio reagem em coro ao tarifaço
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro and the PL reacted in unison on social media to the 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods, repeating the slogan 'The blame is Lula's' after U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio attributed the measure to Lula's posture. Posts from PL profiles, Flávio Bolsonaro, Sóstenes Cavalcante, and Izalci Lucas sought to shift economic blame to the Lula government, citing Rubio’s statement as proof. Some reactions were mocking, such as Nikolas Ferreira’s three-word English remark.

item.title: Redes sociais viram campo de batalha judicial entre campanhas de Tarcísio e Haddad
item.description: The Regional Electoral Court (TRE) ordered the removal of 21 posts and imposed fines in the pre-campaigns of Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad for illegal use of artificial intelligence and irregular boosting. Fernando Haddad's government program coordinator Emídio de Souza (PT), was fined R$10,000 for using synthetic content to alter images of living people. Tarcísio's team accuses Haddad's campaign of systematic defamation through illegal tactics.

item.title: Leia na íntegra pesquisa Quaest sobre o impacto do tarifaço na eleição presidencial
item.description: The Quaest poll shows 51% of Brazilian voters blame Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) for the 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods, while 30% defend him. The tariff increases Lula’s (PT) voting intention to 42%, compared to 27% for Bolsonaro, with a margin of error of two percentage points and a 95% confidence level.

item.title: Taxa dos EUA tem impacto de US$ 11 bi em exportações, diz Amcham
item.description: Amcham Brazil warned that the 25% tariff imposed by the U.S. on Brazilian products could impact over $11 billion in exports from Brazil’s industry and agribusiness, placing Brazil among the most restricted countries for accessing the U.S. market. The measure, stemming from a USTR Section 301 investigation into alleged unfair trade practices — including Pix, digital trade, and illegal deforestation — took effect with exceptions for meat, coffee and other goods. While the exceptions were viewed positively, the group urged continued dialogue between the Brazilian and U.S. governments to reduce economic harm.

item.title: Quaest: maioria concorda com Lula e diz que tarifaço é culpa de Flávio
item.description: A Quaest poll shows most Brazilians agree with President Lula's claim that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro pressured the U.S. government to impose tariffs on Brazilian goods, while Flávio's assertion that he sought the opposite finds little support. The survey, conducted July 10–13 with 2,004 respondents, suggests the Trump tariffs could harm Flávio Bolsonaro's electoral prospects.

item.title: Seção 301: Brasil é laboratório da ferramenta que EUA querem usar para tarifaço 2.0; entenda
item.description: The U.S. announced a 25% tariff on select Brazilian imports effective July 22, based on Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act, citing unfair trade practices including PIX, ethanol access, illegal deforestation, and piracy. Strategic goods like coffee, beef, and aircraft parts were exempted, while ethanol, agricultural machinery, and paper will be taxed. President Lula denounced the tariffs as illegal and arbitrary, stating Brazil will respond via the Economic Reciprocity Law and seek redress through the WTO.

item.title: Boulos atribui tarifaço à “traição” de Flávio
item.description: Guilherme Boulos, chief minister of the Presidency's General Secretariat, blamed the Bolsonaro family — particularly Flávio Bolsonaro — for the 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods, calling it a consequence of their 'betrayal.' In posts on X, he argued Brazil is paying the price for damaged relations under the previous administration.

item.title: Tarifaço: Lula conversa com chanceler brasileiro para avaliar alcance de taxa de 25% imposta pelos EUA
item.description: President Lula and Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira spoke by phone to assess the 25% tariff imposed by the U.S. on Brazilian goods, which they deem unfair and are evaluating countermeasures under the Reciprocity Law. The tariff takes effect on July 22 but exempts key exports such as beef, orange juice, coffee, and ethanol, following a USTR Section 301 investigation into alleged unfair practices, including Brazil’s use of Pix and illegal deforestation.

item.title: O impacto do tarifaço nas intenções de voto de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro, segundo a Quaest
item.description: A Quaest poll shows that the U.S. tariff increase on Brazilian goods raised voting intent for Lula to 42%, up from 39% in June, while support for Flávio Bolsonaro dropped from 30% to 27% overall and eroded even among his base: from 88% to 81% among Bolsonarists and from 70% to 60% in non-Bolsonarista right-wing voters. The survey interviewed 2,004 respondents between July 10–13 with a two-point margin of error.

item.title: Flávio afirma que “nenhum candidato” vai cortar o Bolsa Família
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) stated that no presidential candidate will cut the Bolsa Família program and announced a digital platform to connect beneficiaries with vocational training, microcredit, and public services, aiming to promote financial independence without immediate loss of benefits. He argued the state should act as a safety net, allowing those who leave the program due to informal work or accidents to re-enroll without stigma. The proposal assigns a central role to Caixa Econômica Federal in implementation.

item.title: Com tarifaço, vendas aos EUA encolheram neste ano, mas exportações para outros países crescem com impulso da China
item.description: Brazilian exports to the U.S. fell 13% in the first half of 2026 due to Trump-era tariffs, creating a US$1.5 billion trade deficit. Despite this decline, total Brazilian exports rose 8.7% through May, driven by a 21.6% increase in sales to China and a 12.8% rise to the European Union, reflecting a successful diversification of trade partners.

item.title: Aldo Rebelo volta a reafirmar nome à Presidência pelo DC após ex-ministro do STF chegar a 2% em pesquisa
item.description: Aldo Rebelo reaffirms his presidential candidacy for the DC, even after the party launched Joaquim Barbosa as a replacement due to poor polling performance. Rebelo states that his situation depends on judicial and party convention decisions, while his pre-campaign continues. The internal dispute has caused a party split and threatens judicial action.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: Maioria culpa Flávio Bolsonaro por tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows that most Brazilians blame Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) more than President Lula (PT) for the U.S. tariffs announced on Brazilian products. The findings indicate public perception that Bolsonaro’s statements or actions contributed to the tariff escalation.

item.title: Reação a tarifaço deve centrar em consumidor afetado
item.description: The United States announced new 25% tariffs on various Brazilian products following five high-level talks that failed to reach a technical agreement. Despite the setback, the Brazilian government and business sector must redouble efforts to keep communication channels open and inform American consumers about the measure’s negative impacts, while seeking to expand the list of exempted items. The decision is politically motivated, but this does not justify empty threats by President Lula aimed at electoral gains.

item.title: Chamado de 'tariflávio', Flávio Bolsonaro retuíta Rubio e culpa Lula pelo tarifaço
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a pre-candidate for the Presidency of the Republic, blamed President Lula (PT) for the new tariffs announced by the United States against Brazil, using the term 'tariflávio' in his rhetoric. He retweeted a post by U.S. Senator Marco Rubio to reinforce his criticism.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: Novo tarifaço diminui vontade de eleitores de direita, inclusive bolsonaristas, de votar em Flávio
item.description: The Quaest poll shows that the U.S. tariff hike reduced voting intention for Flávio Bolsonaro among right-wing voters, including both Bolsonarists and non-Bolsonarists, with a 7-point drop among Bolsonarists (from 88% to 81%) and a 10-point decline among non-Bolsonarist right-wing voters (from 70% to 60%). Support for Lula rose among independents, increasing from 26% to 33%, while preference for 'other' candidates rose in parallel. The survey was conducted from July 10–13, prior to the official confirmation of the tariffs by Washington.

item.title: Pré-candidatos à Presidência reagem ao novo tarifaço de Trump
item.description: Presidential pre-candidates for the 2026 election reacted to the new 25% U.S. tariff on most Brazilian goods, condemning the measure and proposing retaliatory actions. Lula (PT) called the tariff unjustified and blamed the Bolsonaro family for worsening trade relations, announcing WTO complaints and domestic protection plans. Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) blamed the Lula government, while Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) and Romeu Zema (Novo) criticized both administrations, warning of sectoral economic damage and poor negotiation conduct.

item.title: Tarifaço: Flávio e Zema atacam Lula, que culpa família Bolsonaro por ação de Trump, enquanto Caiado critica polarização
item.description: The United States' decision to impose a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods starting July 22 sparked a new confrontation in the 2026 presidential race. President Lula (PT) blamed the Bolsonaro family for the trade negotiation outcome, while Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) attacked the federal government, claiming the measure politically benefits Lula. Ronaldo Caiado (União Brasil) and Romeu Zema (Novo) positioned themselves as alternatives, with Caiado criticizing polarization and Zema condemning the PT government’s handling of the negotiations.

item.title: Fiesp culpa governo Lula por tarifaço: 'ruídos diplomáticos desnecessários e críticas personalistas'
item.description: Fiesp blamed the Lula government for the U.S. 25% tariff on Brazilian exports, citing unnecessary diplomatic noise, personal criticisms, and political misalignment with Washington as damaging bilateral relations. The group argued the tariff undermines Brazil’s industrial competitiveness and advocated for a more technical, pragmatic approach to U.S. relations to avoid future trade retaliation.

item.title: A reação da indústria brasileira ao novo tarifaço de Trump
item.description: Brazilian industry expressed concern over the new 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods, arguing it undermines competitiveness and could have been avoided through more technical negotiations. Fiesp and CNI criticized the Lula government’s handling of trade talks, citing a 13% drop in U.S.-bound exports since 2025, particularly in steel, ethanol, and industrial goods. In response, the government announced it would invoke the Reciprocity Law to impose countermeasures, including tariffs on U.S. imports.

item.title: Caiado critica Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro após anúncio de novo tarifaço pelos EUA
item.description: Former Goiás governor and presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) criticized President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) for lacking dialogue capacity in trade negotiations and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) for prioritizing elections over national interests, following the U.S. announcement of a 25% additional tariff on Brazilian goods effective July 22. Caiado warned the tariff could destroy entire economic sectors, especially agribusiness, and accused the government of offering only 'palliative care' amid three commercial attacks on Brazilian agriculture (China, EU, and U.S.).

item.title: JOTA Principal: Novo tarifaço dos EUA reforça discurso eleitoral de Lula respaldado por pesquisas
item.description: The new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods bolster Lula’s electoral narrative of defending national sovereignty, with polls showing public support. The PT campaign attributes the decision to the Bolsonaro clan while preparing economic measures to mitigate impacts. The government’s response will split between political messaging and pending commercial retaliation.

item.title: Convenções partidárias começam em 20 de julho; confira as datas e as regras
item.description: Party conventions for the 2026 elections will take place between July 20 and August 5, defining candidacies and coalitions for majoritarian and proportional offices. The first pre-candidate to hold a convention will be Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) on July 25, followed by Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) on July 26, Romeu Zema (Novo) on July 27, Renan Santos (Mission) on August 1, and Lula on August 2, all in in-person, virtual, or hybrid formats as permitted by party statutes.

item.title: Criado o Dia Nacional da Capoeira, a ser celebrado em 15 de julho
item.description: National Capoeira Day was established to be celebrated on July 15 under Law 15.469, sanctioned by the Presidency of the Republic. The date commemorates the recognition of capoeira as Brazil’s Intangible Cultural Heritage and highlights its role as a cultural resistance practice rooted in the struggles of enslaved Africans, reinforcing national identity and regional diversity.

item.title: Governo rejeita críticas e diz que fez mais de 30 contatos com os EUA para negociar tarifas
item.description: The Brazilian government rejects criticism over the new U.S. tariff, stating it has made over 30 contacts since the original announcement to negotiate a solution, including meetings with Marco Rubio and Jamieson Greer. The measure, set to take effect on July 22, was labeled 'lamentable' by the government, which vows to invoke the reciprocity law. The opposition blames Lula for negotiation failures, while the government attributes the U.S. decision to ideological and political motives.

item.title: Tarifaço: aliado de Flávio vê 'militância ideológica' do governo, que reage ao clã Bolsonaro e cita 'falsos patriotas'
item.description: Allies of pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) accused the Lula government of causing the U.S. tariff hike through an ideologically driven foreign policy that ignored negotiations with Washington and reacted late to trade barriers from China and the EU. Senator Rogério Marinho said the government 'reaps what it sows', while Marcelo Freixo accused Flávio and the Bolsonaro clan of conspiring for electoral gain, labeling them 'false patriots'. The federal government called July 15 a 'lamentable milestone' in Brazil-U.S. relations and pledged to activate reciprocal measures under the Reciprocity Law.

item.title: Nikolas Ferreira ironiza governo Lula após tarifa de 25%: "Make the L"
item.description: Federal Deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-RJ) mocked President Lula's government after the U.S. announced a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, using the phrase 'Make the L' in reference to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who blamed Lula for lacking good faith in negotiations. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) also attacked the government, claiming Lula is leaving the country 'on a plane without a pilot' and accusing him of corruption, incompetence, and vengeance, despite initially advocating for delaying the tariffs until after the 2026 elections.

item.title: O novo gesto de Flávio para tentar ganhar terreno sobre eleitorado feminino
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL's pre-candidate for president, will launch the 'Brazil for Her' plan in a live stream to appeal to female voters, following a public rift with Michelle Bolsonaro and declining support among women. The announcement will feature Daniella Marques, former aide to Paulo Guedes and a potential running mate. The plan, developed after meetings with female PL leaders, aims to regain ground lost with female electorate.

item.title: EE UU impone nuevos aranceles del 25% a gran parte de productos brasileños y acusa a Lula de no negociar “de buena fe”
item.description: The United States has imposed a new 25% tariff on most Brazilian products, accusing Brazil of unfair competition. The Lula administration labeled the move as purely political and announced it will activate the Reciprocity Law to apply equivalent measures on U.S. goods. This tariff escalation is expected to become a central issue in the 2026 Brazilian elections, where Lula will face Flávio Bolsonaro, as a similar move in 2025 had previously boosted the president’s popularity.

item.title: Vídeo: Davi anuncia duas semanas de esforço concentrado após o recesso
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre announced the dates for the concentrated effort to vote on bills during the electoral period: August 10–14 and August 31–September 3. The work will be coordinated with the Chamber of Deputies’ concentrated efforts, as agreed with Chamber President Deputy Hugo Motta.
